notes.title: New year, new difficulty levels!
notes.notes:
Welcome to the first update of 2023!

In this [b]Difficulty Levels Patch[/b] (game version 0.2.7.74) we’ve added [b]2 brand new difficulty levels [/b]to Project Warlock II. Namely:  Come Get Some and Ready to Die. We want to deliver a much more challenging gameplay to those looking for intense, action packed, and deadly (really deadly) experience!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/580f0dee6555cf4ecfd44c77f748b4662b7a417d.jpg[/img]

The Difficulty Levels Patch brings not only new difficulty levels, but also an [b]overall balance[/b] to the two existing ones. Each Difficulty also grants a different score multiplier so if you want to crank those combo scores up, make sure to play on the highest difficulty you can.

[b]Spoiler alert:[/b] This includes mini bosses, so if you’ve encountered an Umbershambler in the past, now he may be accompanied by his Turbo Knight bodyguards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/3c7fa17f34ba4489824846dc21b5ca597b9eec01.png[/img]

Shamblers and Ubershamblers should me more of a threat now thanks to balancing and improvements to their AI.

This patch also brings an [b]overhaul to the music[/b] in the first episode!

Most of the level tracks were reworked and extended - each having almost 10 minutes thanks to Jerry and Luke!

E1M1 is now accompanied by a new music track, titled GATHERUM 5 - it's a great throwback to the music from Project Warlock. We can’t wait to hear your thoughts!

Go and check the new and difficulty levels for yourself and be sure to share your thoughts on the forum and our official Discord! All feedback is welcome and most helpful in improving the game.

As always, please leave a Steam review if you enjoy the game as it helps us in reaching new players.

That’s all for today’s update, we’d like to wish you a Happy New Year filled with wonderful adventures!

notes.title: Help us balance the new difficulty levels
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

We’re hard at work on implementing new difficulty levels to the game and we could use your help to make sure that they’re well-balanced and challenging.
 
[b]We plan to introduce four difficulty levels:[/b] Walk in the Park, Moderate Rumble, Come Get Some, and the most challenging Ready to Die. The main difference between them will be made through the number of enemies and their higher stats. Enemies will have more health, and resistance, and deal more damage to the player.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/580f0dee6555cf4ecfd44c77f748b4662b7a417d.jpg[/img]

Before these new settings become part of Project Warlock II, you can check them out on a dedicated Beta branch and share your feedback in the comments or [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1640300/discussions/0/3712685859921918649/]this forum thread[/url].
 
[h3]How can you join this playtest?[/h3]

Be sure to save your game first! Once you switch to the Beta branch, in-game autosaves will be overwritten, so [b]make sure to save your progress with a manual save option[/b].

In the Steam client, right-click on the game title, go to Properties, then to the Beta section, and select [b]difficulty_level_test - Difficulty Level Test Beta Branch[/b] from the expandable list. This will install the [b]build version 0.2.7.73[/b]. Start a new game and select one of four difficulty levels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/4348e8257a7fa67a62a11d02c8447d7978e5f1a8.jpg[/img]

Once you’re done playing the Difficulty Level Test build, make sure to switch back from the beta branch to the main game branch in Steam’s properties. All game saves made during this playtest will be incompatible with the default game build, including autosaves!

The beta branch with the [b]Difficulty Level Test will stay active for the next two weeks, until December 27[/b]. We hope you’ll find some time to give it a try and share your feedback with us in the comments, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1640300/discussions/0/3712685859921918649/]in this forum thread[/url], or directly on [url=https://discord.com/invite/Nx6CmMNgrj]our official Discord[/url].

notes.title: Time to make a split
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, 

We’re happy to finally share with you this [b]major update for Chapter 1 of Project Warlock II[/b]. 

In this Level Patch (game version 0.2.7.51), we took the original six levels, split them, and rebuilt them into twelve completely revamped ones. They’re more streamlined, easier to navigate, and full of challenges. This wouldn’t be possible without your comments and feedback after playing the Early Access version and participating in our closed playtesting sessions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/0b8603c814367643c20ff48801d8d5cadeefba20.png[/img]

This patch also marks [b]a major shift in the direction in which we want to take Project Warlock II[/b]. 

Your feedback made it clear that there are some areas from the original Project Warlock that you miss quite a lot. This convinced us to not only look for new solutions but also try to bring back and expand the mechanics that we all enjoyed in the previous game. 

For example, we’re currently hard at work ironing out a perk system that will allow for bigger customization of your gameplay. These changes will have a significant impact on our roadmap and previously announced updates like reworking the weapons system. We’ll share an updated roadmap along with the next patch as it’s still under construction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/951b960894721283a7ac21e00c68b9f870b44aa2.png[/img]
[i]Work in progress look at the new Perk Shop   
[/i]

While Luke and Jerry are reworking, extending, and modifying the music to make it fit the new levels, we've already updated some tracks in this patch and added some new, unused tracks for you to listen to and make your play more fun. We're aiming at a tasteful combination of ambient and melody within each level's score. Please note that a major music rework update is yet to come!

For now, let’s get back to the Level Patch and have a look at [b]the list of levels in Chapter 1[/b]:

[b]E1M1[/b] - Siege of Palmer's Castle
[b]E1M2[/b] - The Obliterated Dungeons
[b]E1M3[/b] - Outskirts of the Munville Forest
[b]E1M4[/b] - The Fall of Darkville
[b]E1M5[/b] - Wretched Ruins of Templepass
[b]E1M6[/b] - Obelisks of Torment
[b]E1M7[/b] - Circle Of Life and Death
[b]E1M8[/b] - Deathly Halls of Undergate
[b]E1M9[/b] - The Depths of Longforgotten
[b]E1M10[/b] - The Titan Apex
[b]E1M11[/b] - Wicked Castle Remains
[b]E1M12[/b] - The Ethereal Abyss

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/6fc48c723fd3d56e4640290709f42667babfdf52.png[/img]
[i]New intro graphics for the levels
[/i]

12 levels now become our new standard and you can expect similar numbers in the upcoming Urd’s Redemption campaign and the yet untitled Chapter 3.

One more disclaimer is needed here. The original Level 5 didn’t meet your expectations and continuously underperformed in our internal playtests. It resulted in a decision to remove it from the game completely. We’ll yet to see if it returns in some shape or form in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/3900780b1402019dee87918a5890dd4d6fd39d02.png[/img]

[b]Please note that due to the changes to the structure of levels in the game, all previous game saves became incompatible with this and future versions of Project Warlock II Early Access![/b]

Below please find [b]the full changelog of the Level Patch[/b]:

GLOBAL CHANGES
[list]
[*] Split the existing levels into 12 levels
[*] Removed level 5 completely
[*] Overall navigation improvements
[*] Simplified level flow with a more linear level progress path
[*] More items spawn in every level
[*] Miniboss encounters are now much more frequent
[*] More big monster encounters
[*] Removed some of the monster spawners spawning behind the player but NOT ALL as it's a design choice in some places
[*] Enlarged a lot of areas to make the movement easier when fighting monsters
[*] Improved various particle effects
[*] Changed and added more music tracks
[/list]

ADDITIONS 
[list]
[*] Added new bestiary entries for elite monsters (Turbo Knight, Skeletron, Hogdaddy, Ubershambler)
[*] Added new secret cameos
[*] Added new entering graphics for each level
[*] Added new Lava Shader
[*] Added new Water Shader
[*] Added new Goo Shader
[*] Added new glowing material to destructible goo elements
[*] Added new 3D explosion effects and particles
[/list]

BALANCE 
[list]
[*] Improved Necrogirls resurrection logic - they will now run toward the resurrected monster
[*] Increased Skeletron projectile speed from 30m/s to 40m/s 
[/list]

BUGFIXES
[list]
[*] Fixed monster landing animation issues
[/list]

KNOW ISSUES (yet to be fixed)
[list]
[*] Ghouls at the tops of the pillars in E1M11 can get stuck even after aggroing the Player
[*] Minimap highlights blocked areas as reachable by the Player
[*] Projectiles of Laser Rifle's Railgun upgrade may be missaligned with the crosshair/gun model
[*] Monsters can be counted incorrectly in the intermission screen on some levels (up and down)
[*] Human NPC kills can count towards total monster kills counter
[/list]

notes.title: New hotfix & Roadmap Update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! 

We’ve released a hotfix that updates the game to [b]version 0.2.6.45[/b] and includes:
[list]
[*] A possible fix where sometimes the explosion VFX would not appear 
[*] Fixed a bug where monsters would aggro at the player too early 
[*] Added autosave-based checkpoints to the Single Stage mode
[/list]
Now you can continue to play your Single Stage run from the last checkpoint after you die on the map. It’s not possible to save, exit, and return to your run later on as they’re intended to serve as one-time only (erm, single) challenges that can be replayed on and on.

We also want to give you a quick development progress update. First, check out the [b]updated 2022 roadmap[/b]. We’re slowly putting more and more check marks on this board! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/8e66ff89aeef401c1d7dc118f86ee54c96b95674.png[/img]

We’re getting closer to a [b]major overhaul of the levels’ structure[/b]. We want to divide them into more, but smaller levels. The total scale and scope of the game will not change, but the flow of every single stage should be more natural and true to Project Warlock's roots. 

[b]Weapons tuning[/b] is another major update that the team has been working on. The basic weapons and both their upgrades and the way the system works will be revamped. The idea behind this update is to remove the feeling of choosing a "downgrade" instead of an upgrade (if you buy a specific upgrade that changes the weapon and you feel like it's not as cool as the base version). Also, we will be splitting weapon upgrades into weapon-specific and universal ones. It’s still early in the works, so your feedback will help us shape it further!

You can also expect Jerry and Luke, the guys behind the first Project Warlock’s OST, to continue their work on making sure that [b]Project Warlock II’s soundtrack is getting bigger and better[/b]. The division of the game's levels into smaller ones will result in additional tracks being added and will result in new tunes to accompany the pixelated slaughter.  

We’re also working our way up the ladder to share the info on [b]the second episode of Project Warlock I[/b]I - and can't wait to hear your thoughts on that!

Thank you to everyone who has already played the Early Access of Project Warlock II and please keep the feedback coming! Be sure to [b]leave a Steam review if you like the game[/b] and recommend us to your friends!

PS. We recently announced a special limited edition Big Box of the original Project Warlock made in cooperation with John Romero himself! Check it out below and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/893680/view/3405303823637108996]head over here[/url] for more details.

notes.title: The stage is set
notes.notes:
Hey all!

Welcome to the first major content patch for Project Warlock II Early Access!

As always, thanks for the constant feedback, comments, messages, [url=https://discord.gg/ensxn8yTvd]Discord[/url] chats, and Steam reviews as they help us shape Project Warlock II into a better game. Please keep them coming!

As we have mentioned in the latest patch notes:

[b]All game saves will become incompatible with new versions of Project Warlock II starting with this update[/b]

It’s a necessary downside of how the game’s structure is changing during the Early Access.

Moving onto the changelog, it is a big one, so buckle up.

notes.title: Upcoming patch details, popular questions answered
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

New patch is playtested at this very moment, and will be available shortly. Below you’ll get a taste of what you can expect in that. Also - we pulled the most popular [b]Project Warlock II[/b] questions from Steam and [url=https://discord.gg/ensxn8yTvd]Discord[/url] and answered those here. 

Since we launched the Early Access version of [b]Project Warlock II[/b] we’ve received a ton of feedback from you, released a number of patches and fixes, as well as revealed our roadmap until the end of the year. And there’s still a lot more to come!

Some of the areas of the game we’re working on are:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/43631d720cc721a2a20c5296d5ca54da77cc5e96.jpg[/img]
[i]Totally redesigned saves system for clearer designation of all saved games, and limiting the number of manual saves and quicksaves[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/395c7299f648f038bf6c5be70b10e59ef3ef8c86.jpg[/img]
[i]Introducing Single Stage mode for revisiting previously completed levels[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/8fd9bcf81af2b9897da3e18f9a76927c175bb20d.jpg[/img]
[i]Adding more pronounced audio and visual cues to enemy demons spawning in[/i]

That and a whole variety of balances, fixes and adjustments across the board that will be fully outlined in the upcoming patch update.  

Each and every suggestion or a bit of feedback provided by you makes its way to our internal database and is reviewed case-by-case. When we said we want to shape the game according to your feedback, we meant it. 

It’s not always possible to respond to all messages or comments and some of them might tackle topics that we’re already aware of and work on, so we’ve prepared this handy list of responses and updates about some of the most frequent topics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/55a53b738addb565575dd6503504be8b4bf6894d.gif[/img]

[b]1:[/b] There’s a lot of clutter on the screen - specifically cooldown reduction orbs, ammo, health, and armor, but also some environment elements sometimes make it hard to see what’s happening on the screen. Are you planning to address that?

[b]ANSWER:[/b] In one of the upcoming patches (coming: soon) we’re reducing the number of dropped items. We’re also repositioning some of the trees as they have been reported to obscure enemies, who (being vicious demons from hell) predictably used that to their advantage. 

[b]2:[/b] Enemies are sometimes getting stuck in walls, trees, pillars, and other elements of the environment. What gives?

[b]ANSWER:[/b] These issues are two-fold. One - after one of the redesigns of the levels, some of the enemies seemed to be stuck in walls with their spawners. Two - some of the doors and breakable passageways cause enemies to behave strangely. The placement issue has been resolved in the latest hotfix patch as well as the enemies getting stuck.

[b]3:[/b] Why are some enemies shooting through the walls?

[b]ANSWER:[/b] This was an issue with misplaced spawners of some monsters. It has now been resolved in the latest  hotfix.

[b]4:[/b] Enemies are getting stuck in the floor - mostly in E1M5.

[b]ANSWER:[/b] This issue has been addressed in the latest patch, we’ve modified the size of the space with problematic floor material.

[b]5:[/b] Sometimes the player character gets stuck on the stairs, slopes, and walls.

[b]ANSWER:[/b] That was an issue with the Player controller and has now been resolved in the latest hotfix. Special thanks to those who attached images or videos of problematic spots in their feedback posts. You know who you are, and we know not all of you wear capes!

[b]6:[/b] The enemies spawning behind the player after picking up every key/weapon/spell are a problem.

[b]ANSWER:[/b] The upcoming patch has more pronounced visual and audio cues to make the monsters spawning in more noticeable as per the screen on top of this post. That same upcoming patch will also result in a do-over regarding the monster spawn placements. The aim is to eradicate those instances that feel unfair to the player by not giving ample time to react. 

[b]7:[/b] The levels are bigger than in the original [b]Project Warlock[/b], which makes them difficult to navigate through and it’s very easy to get lost and wander in circles.

[b]ANSWER:[/b] We’re looking at the scope of the levels and making sure they are more accessible. One thing that emerged from the playtest and subsequent feedback is that we will be going for a division of the levels into smaller and more approachable areas. This is coming in the future.

[b]8:[/b] Some of the secrets are too hard to find.

[b]ANSWER:[/b] Well… yes and no. We believe that most of the secrets aren’t that problematic and are well-indicated, whether by a red target mark, a button, or a destructible wall. But we’ve heard a lot of voices. In the previous point, we’ve mentioned redesigning the levels. We believe it will help this issue as the levels will be smaller and secrets should become easier to find. 

Also, the Single Stage Mode (coming in the next content patch) will allow players to jump between levels to find secrets they’ve missed.

[b]9:[/b] Are more game modes coming to [b]PW2[/b]?

[b]ANSWER:[/b] Yes. Single Stage mode is now being extensively tested and will be a part of the next content patch. Stars of one of the future updates - the Mutators will also have a significant impact on the way you play the game.

[b]10:[/b] The music in [b]Project Warlock II[/b] feels repetitive and just not that good, whereas it was one of the best things in the original [b]Project Warlock[/b].

[b]ANSWER:[/b] Jerry and Luke - the guys behind the first [b]Project Warlock[/b]’s OST are hard at work on making sure that [b]Project Warlock II[/b]’s soundtrack is as memorable - or waaaay more - as that of the first game. The issue with the tracks right now is that the concept for dynamic music that was originally in place had to be reconsidered. It just didn’t work that well and was changed. Currently, some of the tracks might need that extra ooomph, but that's because most of them are devoid of their more dynamic, combat parts. There will be new tracks, as we’re working on the [b]PW2[/b] soundtrack to hit the bar we’ve set with the original game. Adding the tracks as well as dividing the levels into smaller parts should reduce the feeling of repetitiveness. 

[b]11:[/b] The loading times in [b]Project Warlock II[/b] seem excessively long, what’s going on?

[b]ANSWER:[/b] We’ve got a two-part fix planned for this. First, in one of the upcoming patches, we’re improving the overall optimization of the levels. Secondly, the loading times will be shorter once we divide the levels. There’s also a topic of the overabundance of saves that also has an impact on this. Upcoming patch addresses that by limiting the number of manual and quicksaves and also by redesigning the save menu. 

One important thing to note here, though. The upcoming patch will render all the saves up until that point useless. So if you want to finish up that playthrough with your current save - now's the right time.    

[b]12:[/b] Some of the weapons and their upgrades feel lackluster.

[b]ANSWER:[/b] Weapon tuning is one of the major updates that the team has been working on for the past couple of months. It will require quite a bit of testing so we have no timeframe to give, but this will be happening very soon. If you'd like to give it a go - please apply for a playtesting role on our [url=https://discord.gg/ensxn8yTvd]Discord[/url] to participate.

In the Weapon update basic weapons and both their upgrades and the way the system works will be revamped. For example, instead of upgrading the Rifle into the Heavy Rifle, you’ll be able to add an additional barrel, sight and ammo capacity. This will result in a chance to expand the capacities of a particular weapon more significantly than just with a short upgrade tree. As we said, it’s early in the works, so your feedback will help us shape it further!

[b]13:[/b] The automap is hard to read, any plans to address that?

[b]ANSWER:[/b] In the upcoming patch, we’ll adjust the minimap’s height colors. More specifically by removing Red and Green height differences, making uncovered terrain white and covered terrain dark gray. This will help you navigate through the levels and find areas you haven’t explored yet. We’ll continue to closely monitor your feedback to make sure we get it right.

[b]14:[/b] When can we expect more levels?

[b]ANSWER:[/b] New levels are coming in the second episode. We don’t have a specific time frame yet, but you can check out our roadmap for 2022 below. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/0e79ec91ccf680d117484788711e35673f6febb3.png[/img]

Thanks for being here with us and look out for the incoming patch!

notes.title: Check what’s next for Project Warlock II
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

Thank you for all the feedback that you keep sharing with us on Steam forums, our official Discord, and directly. Early Access of Project Warlock II has only just started but [b]our team is hard at work on Chapter 2 and improving the game overall[/b]. 

Before the release, we’ve spent over six months playtesting Project Warlock II with both internal and external QA teams, Kickstarter backers, and selected Discord users. The Early Access launch has brought [b]an influx of a completely fresh perspective on the game[/b] with your forum comments, Discord messages, and over 150 Steam reviews. Some of them were pretty detailed and probably most helpful in identifying issues to address. We’re grateful for each and every piece of feedback that you decided to share, and please keep it coming!

While we’re pretty sure we won’t be able to satisfy everyone as opinions always differ, just like some like DOOM more than Quake, and otherwise. Still, [b]our main goal right now[/b] is to find the right balance between the new ideas, building upon the original game, and addressing some of your most voiced requests for changes. 

With that in mind, we want to share with you [b]our 2022 roadmap for the game[/b]: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/0e79ec91ccf680d117484788711e35673f6febb3.png[/img]

We want to complete this roadmap by the end of the year, updating it as we go and then providing the next one. At the same time, we’re keeping room for potential patches, fixes, and updates that might be needed along the way. We already [b]had our first two patches released[/b], adding a highly requested reload option, nerfing down the Necrogirl, and adding various visual and gameplay fixes, and with lots more to come.

We’d also like you to know what you can expect from the game content-wise. [b]A Single Stage option, as well as two additional difficulty levels[/b], will be introduced in the near future. Weapons rebalancing and modifications are to follow. These will offer deeper customization options for the guns allowing you to upgrade your favorite tools of destruction further.

Given the nature of Early Access, [b]almost every aspect of the game can be subject to change[/b] or at least a deeper discussion between you and the developers. We want to run the most significant and impactful changes through you. Soon you’ll be able to access and comment on beta branch builds with experimental versions of changes like the overhauled weapons system, new Single Stage mode, and Photo Mode. Follow our channels for updates on when these will become available.

A lot of stuff is happening, and the whole team is very happy and motivated by your reception, even if a bit tired with the amount of work. Still, one of the highlights of recent weeks was [b]the endorsement we got from our personal hero[/b], one of the creators of DOOM, John Romero himself.  

[previewyoutube=ZLk7EMOzceY;full][/previewyoutube]

If you’re new to Project Warlock II, there are also these helpful game guides published by [b]TheGamer[/b] that we highly recommend - be sure to [url=https://www.thegamer.com/project-warlock-2-tips-and-tricks/]start with this one[/url]. You should also check [b]Under The Mayo[/b]’s in-depth first look at the game before playing.

[previewyoutube=FC9t6nGko4Y;full][/previewyoutube]

Finally, if you haven’t already, then please consider grabbing one of our [b]special Project Warlock II bundles[/b] with extra discounts for the original game and cool titles from our indie developer friends. 

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/26638/Project_Warlock_1_&_2/

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/26602/ULTRAKILL_x_Project_Warlock_2/   

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/26600/POSTAL_Brain_Damaged_x_Project_Warlock_2/ 

Thank you, enjoy the game, share it with your friends, send us your feedback, and [b]leave a review on Steam[/b] to help us reach more players. 

See you next time!

notes.notes:
[b]Project Warlock II is now available to play in Early Access![/b]
  
Five years ago, when [b]Project Warlock[/b] launched, it was already envisioned as the first part of the trilogy, and though 2018 seems like forever ago, we are now nearing the second step on that journey. And that one starts with a baby step for Palmer – the first of the three Warlocks to grace the game.
 
To get you in the right mood, we used one of the new tools you’ll get to use yourself in a matter of months. [b]Photo Mode[/b] - currently in the testing phase - will allow you to craft your videos to the soundtrack of your choosing. And what better way to show a glimpse of the power of this tool than in our very own [b]Project Warlock II Early Access launch trailer[/b]. In all, it’s 100% in-game captured footage glory.  

[previewyoutube=-b6PmphIwwQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Hopefully, by this time, you’re either a Backer or already have made up your mind to buy [b]Project Warlock II[/b], but let's assume you still need some convincing. And instead of us - let’s pass the mic over to one of the people responsible for the fact that a game like Project Warlock can even exist. So, without further ado – take it away, John.

[previewyoutube=ZLk7EMOzceY;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Project Warlock II[/b] is a much more complex game than its predecessor, but talking about this seems kind of redundant with the first chapter of the game now available to play. So, grab the game with a launch discount or from one of the three bundles with even better offers.
 
The first Bundle comes courtesy of the Early Access behemoth – the super smooth, sexy [b]ULTRAKILL[/b] from the retro shooter powerhouse New Blood Interactive.

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/26602/ULTRAKILL_x_Project_Warlock_2/ 

The second in line is the new dude on the block bundle. Only the dude smokes, the block is pissed all over, and a cat is running for his life in the recently released [b]POSTAL: Brain Damaged[/b] by the fellow Poles at Hyperstrange.

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/26600/POSTAL_Brain_Damaged_x_Project_Warlock_2/

Last but not least is the [b]Project Warlock I & II combo[/b] for those who never had the chance to play the first game and would like to give it a go.

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/26638/Project_Warlock_1_&_2/

This is just the beginning and we hope you'll join us on this ride and share your feedback on the forum and [url=https://discord.com/invite/Nx6CmMNgrj]our Discord[/url]. Leave a review if you like it, and stay tuned for more!

We’re coming to you with another Dev Update. This one will be quick and short, but we still wanted to check-in, as it has become our monthly tradition.

We’re getting closer and closer to having the game ready for you to play. We’ve spent the last weeks getting a build ready for playtesting. This included polishing the game, balancing and tuning enemies, weapons, loot, whatever you could think of. It’s the last stretch before Early Access, so… we’re getting there.

We also have a neat surprise. Meet PIG DADDY, a new monster type coming to Project Warlock II. We can’t wait for you to see him in action!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/baf084fe8f22fe319d9479ad6c4b644edd2035fe.gif[/img]

As always, please follow and wishlist Project Warlock II, and spread the word. Make sure to join our [url=https://discord.com/invite/ensxn8yTvd]official Discord [/url]to share your feedback and thoughts about our game!

See you next time!

notes.title: New hellspawn and even more destruction!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

It’s a brand new year, so it’s time for some fresh dev update about [b]Project Warlock II[/b]. The game's development is in full swing and you can see some of the things that we were working on throughout the Holiday season and beyond. 

We’d like to start off by thanking everyone who joined our streams during the Winter Sale and on Twitch where Kuba presented the latest updates to the game. We also have the videos below, for those who’ve missed them. 

[previewyoutube=o1U44Q6xo8w;full][/previewyoutube]

[previewyoutube=BQutcprui4M;full][LiveDev stream link][/previewyoutube]

Now let’s talk about some [b]new monsters[/b]. This time we’ve got two new types of demons straight from hell to show you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/f236f6f1cf5f8304c5af63d3eb3a1bd0b90a1762.gif[/img]

The [b]Assassin[/b] and the [b]Necrogirl[/b] are still work-in-progress, so let us know what you think!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/d88cb485a5343d45b6e3a1f4a7c9b9f300998ee5.gif[/img]

We’re also taking the destruction to the next level by adding the ability to [b]destroy environments[/b] using guns at your disposal. We hope it will make the gameplay more interesting and fun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/ac1cc26a0e6f27b9737e50d4e34b5db4ac35d0e1.gif[/img]

The [b]UI changes[/b] are another thing on display. We’re working on a brand new interface for the map and Bestiary. These should provide much more clarity and also look much, much better.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/8c70470b2692c876eb0f3f8397eb24dfc8b2eec4.png[/img]

These should provide much more clarity than their predecessors and also look much, much better.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/471c1f606a3216e8e4bc13574458794d6d76e2de.png[/img]

Apart from the new things, we’ve also made a round of balance changes and tinkered quite a bit in level design. 

We’re constantly trying to squeeze out as much from our ideas as we can and appreciate all your comments and feedback both here and [url=https://discord.gg/ensxn8yTvd]on Discord[/url].  

See you next time!

notes.title: Of monsters and pickups
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

While visually overhauling the monsters based on your feedback, our lead artist David decided to give those minions of hell that little bit more protection. 

Arm pads. Pieces of mail. Metal plates. All bolted or sewn to their inhuman, otherworldly flesh. As if their gnashing teeth, boney spikes protruding from their thick hides and huge, saber-like talons weren’t enough. But it's not like the odds are fully stacked against you. The newest build update sees Palmer on the chase for newly added, differently colored armor sets strewn around the levels, or armor shards laying out and about.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/9fa1528bcfc29871a6d0f2879516da77d76ed6a6.png[/img]
[i]What's blue and gold and makes chingy sound[/i]

[b]LET ME INTRODUCE MYSELF[/b]
Each of the monsters in Project Warlock II is breathing, jumping, shooting, swiping, and or rushing fiend that has a thing for Palmer. That "thing" can mean they can enter a frenzy and rush Palmer head-on. Or fire rockets anticipating where you will be in the next second or two. They can also – as is the case with the new, revamped Imp – anticipate your own shots with a slower projectile weapon. And unless you get close enough to slash them with a sword or blast them both barrels point-blank - that can be the difference between getting them and getting owned.

In short: you'll have to understand those enemies to emerge successfully from each encounter. But we still felt something was missing. Namely - a proper introduction to our nameless, unfriendly minions that you will learn to take care of. To remedy that – each new monster that you face will have his or her intro vignette that will help you flesh out their character. Here’s a WIP clip for Imp.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/55a53b738addb565575dd6503504be8b4bf6894d.gif[/img]
[i]The first pass on the Imp's intro[/i]

[b]CODEX ENTRIES[/b]
While on the topic of introductions. Since the Warlock’s levels are way bigger than ever before, it felt fitting to make sure there’s enough to do there when it came to both the enemies, secrets, and collectibles. One of the new items you will get to pick up when traversing the dark world that fell under the spell of the Necromancer is the Codex entry scroll.

These dark parchments hide the information that will help you understand and take advantage of the traits of a given monster and will be readily available to view in the menu. Sometimes the scrolls are laying there in plain sight, but sometimes you will have to take an extra route and do a little searching to find them and seize the monstrous secrets they hold.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/b64bc56491891dbee600e33ad5bf64d869327a75.png[/img]
[i]Biro's sketches that served as the basis of Codex entries visuals[/i]

[b]BONEY WILL MISS YOU (NOW)[/b]
Since we’re in what can be tentatively called the “Monster part of the update” let’s briefly touch upon behavior patterns of one particular enemy. One that seemed to evoke a lot of emotions from everyone that had the opportunity to meet Boney in the demo. In the Boney-specific manner, that is: getting it scanned by his shotgun blast from as of yet unseen position.

There’s this less-known movie from the ’90s starring Dennis Quaid and Louis Gossett Jr. called “Enemy Mine". It’s a story of a human space fighter pilot and his alien counterpart. Both participate in space dogfights and both end up stranded on the planet below. They begin as mortal enemies only to find humanity (alienity?) in each other and become friends for life.

This story is here to anchor the fact that there is no human possibility for anyone to go from hate to love in the Palmer-Boney relationship. And since it could get annoying especially on the supposedly more forgiving lower difficulty levels – the sniping skills of our emaciated sniper have been nerfed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/eb87130daf3258613de7921bbc031898d4477b36.png[/img]
[i]The Boney you will learn to like[/i]

[b]THE DROP BONANZA[/b]
Currently, the number of drops from the enemies is being tweaked to make sure that each level provides the promised challenge. Vials of blood refilling health bar, cooldown tokens dropping as a result of successful combos helping recharge those spells faster, or shards of different colored armors restoring them to their pristine condition. All of these – in specific circumstances – have a tendency to fill out the screen if unchecked. Below is a sample of what that means. Spoiler: this one stays.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/1cc52b6c71419be3c124f6686995cc208a60e0bf.gif[/img]
[i]No, this is a perfectly appropriate amount of drops [/i]

[b]DOUBLE STAFFING[/b]
The first spell/cooldown skill you pick up in Project Warlock II is Akimbo. You can check it in the demo for that immensely satisfying effect of doubling down on the ammo consumption and non-neglectable damage output. Or – to put it more bluntly – this allows you to absolutely obliterate enemy stupid enough to get in your way when you brandish that Harvester and decide to magically CTRL+V that weapon to another hand. 

Up until the demo, the staffs and swords were not yet using the skill to their desired effect. But recently the staff got their own looping attack animation so that the poor monsters are literally standing no chance to the onslaught of the magic spewing from the two powerful staves.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/54105b0de9bf9b8a576836b469a59cbc88c05822.gif[/img]
[i]Staff Akimbo applied to staff's Fire upgrade[/i]

For more updates about the game, follow us on Steam and join [url=https://discord.gg/ensxn8yTvd]our official Discord[/url]. Remember to wishlist the game, and tell your friends.

See you next time!

notes.title: Community Q&A - you asked and we answered!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

Recently we've run a community survey on Kickstarter and our [url=https://discord.gg/ensxn8yTvd]official Discord[/url]. We got some questions along with your feedback, so we sat down with Kuba, the designer, programmer, and creative mind behind Project Warlock II to answer them for you below. 

[b]When do you expect the early access and full versions of Project Warlock II will be released?[/b]

We’re aiming for early 2022 with Early Access but it’s too soon to commit to a specific date. There’s still a lot of feedback from gamers that we want to implement before sharing the 1st chapter (Palmer’s World). Once the Early Access starts, the work on chapter 2 will continue alongside tweaks and updates to the first one. And then we’re on to the third chapter. The full release of Project Warlock II will come once all three chapters are ready.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/f0650abea46cc851bfe3c83bb303eb290a762b4c.gif[/img]
[i]Doing some carnage while testing the game[/i]

[b]How is Project Warlock II changing based on demo feedback?[/b]

We’ve made substantial changes to the level design, monster design, and texture work. The game resembles the original PW graphics more than ever before. We’ve also added new graphical interfaces and new Quality of Life features such as keybindings. The list is huge and we plan to test these upgrades during extensive playtesting sessions in December.

[b]What inspired you to make Project Warlock?[/b]

As an aspiring game dev, I had tons of unfinished projects. I made horror games, driving games, and first-person shooters. At one point, I felt like making FPS games is what I really want. I understood what makes a good FPS, so I decided to put that knowledge to good use. Project Warlock had a couple of different names before but the concept of a Wolf3D dungeon-crawler with simple RPG elements was always there :)

[b]How did you manage this whole project basically on your own? Who else do you work with?[/b]

First of all, I had to set a scope of the project and only do stuff that I was 100% sure I was capable of. This is the key to success in my opinion. Other than that, it’s important to set certain boundaries when designing the game according to your capabilities. That way you can avoid promising stuff that you can’t work out!

I also work with Dawid Korzekwa (Lead Artist), Jerry Lehr (Musician), Luke Wilson (Musician), Bogdan Biro (Artist), Piotr Niedzielski (Sound Designer) - that’s the core development team of Project Warlock II.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/4ea300670f78f8bb3474eca4a49119f7df805418.png[/img]
[i]Project Warlock II dev team. Top from the left: Kuba, Jerry, and Piotr. Down from the left: Luke, Dawid, and Bogdan[/i].

[b]How did you decide on the games' visual style?[/b]

In the original Project Warlock, we wanted something unique yet simple, because when making your first game you shouldn’t create unnecessary obstacles. We knew that drawing a lot of different sprites with complicated colors would make things difficult, so Dawid thought about using the Commodore 64 color palette. In PW2 we’re expanding on the style that Dawid created and trying to define our own color palette.

[b]I absolutely love the first game but so far PW2 looks like it's going to make PW1 almost obsolete. How can the first game stay exciting and relevant with all this awesome stuff coming in PW2?[/b]

PW will never be obsolete because PW2 is a real sequel, a new chapter that expands the fun instead of being identical to PW. Still, there will be noticeable differences and upgrades in both gameplay and visuals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/e71dff8e5c5a19bdde8cf6e052188563eb1251a6.png[/img]
[i]One of the levels in the first chapter of Project Warlock II[/i]

[b]Will the three warlocks have their own different campaigns/stories with their own unique levels or will it be just one campaign and you choose which warlock you want to play as? Or will it be one campaign and you play as the three warlocks throughout it?[/b]

Each Warlock is going to have their own campaign with different levels and stories (lore).

[b]Are there any plans for using warlocks outside of their specific campaigns? For example, using Urd in Palmer's campaign?[/b]

This is something we have thought about and might come back to in the future. First, we want to balance and finish all the episodes separately.

[b]Are there any plans to add the original warlock as a playable character to PWII?[/b]

Can’t answer that question!

[b]Any plans for mod support?[/b]

Would really love to! We’ll see what the future brings. I am not crossing it out, however, it’s not our main focus.

[b]Any plans for console ports/releases?[/b]

Definitely!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/62ef5f3f08bab9db0ccd77a8755968afe9d895c7.png[/img]
[i]Look out for these spikes while dodging![/i]

[b]What is your opinion on the Early Access model? Do you think it leads to better games? Is it necessary to secure operating funds for indie devs or a useful way to steer development?[/b]

It really depends on the developer. For me, it’s important to get feedback from players throughout the development process. This way it’s easier to adjust certain parts of the game rather than patching a complete product.

[b]What are your favorite FPS campaigns in the last few years?[/b]

I have to say, I really liked the story in Far Cry 6.  The world is so beautiful and just fits me very well, because I love Cuba and the Spanish language. Other than that, I also liked Call of Duty: Modern Warfare’s (2019) single-player campaign, and obviously both Wolfenstein: The New Order and The New Colossus as well.

[b]Do you have any games that you shouldn't enjoy because of your preferences but you actually really like them?[/b]

I’m not a huge fan of League of Legends but I really enjoy playing it from time to time. Also, Arcane is lit AF!

[b]Are there any other gaming genres that you would like to develop apart from FPS?[/b]

I really like driving games, so making one would be pretty interesting for me. 
But I mainly want to develop FPS games.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/22a336d61ac293c4e0083f5a700aa5a0fcfa37b2.png[/img]
[i]Soon this arena will fill out with enemies![/i]

[b]What do you consider to be the most difficult thing about creating a game?[/b]

I see a lot of good games with awesome lore, great visuals, and sound that fall short in the mechanics department, like animation fluidity, movement, weapon weight, recoil, weapon bob, etc. Nailing the gameplay mechanics, the feeling of movement, gunplay, and making the gameplay-loop engaging are by far the hardest things to develop in my opinion. This is not something you can create easily - you need to feel it.

[b]If speaking to a total newcomer to game development, what would you advise interested parties to consider? From game ideas to learning developer work, does one steer the other?[/b]

I think the most important thing is to start simple. With additional experience, you’ll start noticing things that you could have done better and you can start improving on yourself. Don’t be shy if something doesn’t work as expected. Just keep trying!

I think one should start with an idea, then try to make a document and describe what this should be exactly and try to tackle all game-related topics in it, like how certain gameplay mechanics should work, etc. Otherwise, you might come to the famous "wall" of gamedev at one point - asking yourself "what should I do next?". This makes you want to stop working on the project and is the main reason why I have so many unfinished projects.

Once you start creating stuff and sharing it online, you’ll start meeting new people. That is one of the best things ever!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/fdc98122830d711b19cec779f8a76f9222a6b476.gif[/img]
[i]Pass through this guard for the final answers...[/i]

[b]How many licks does it take to get to the center of a tootsie roll pop?[/b]

One good bite :)

[b]Will you be making any more FPS games after this one? Will there be Warlock III?[/b]

Project Warlock was always planned as a trilogy, and I still want to keep it that way. 

[b]If PW2 is set between Doom and Quake mechanically, where would you want to go with PW3?[/b]

I believe that 2D sprites in a 3D world really give a certain satisfaction when playing. It just feels so right, crisp, and fitting. I’d definitely want to improve on that. We’re constantly learning how to streamline the sprite-creation process more effectively. 

PW3 might be an even more interesting evolution of PW2. I definitely don’t want to make PW3 look and feel like PW2 - otherwise, I could just make a DLC for PW2 instead of a new title.

[b]Quake or Unreal?[/b]

Why not both!? I’ve spent more time with Quake 3 Arena tbh :D But love both series anyways <3


Follow us for more updates and see you next time!

notes.title: The many faces of Project Warlock II
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

[b]Timeline update:[/b] Project Warlock II is nearing the content lock of the game's first Episode - Palmer's World in the coming weeks. After that, we're heading into an extensive playtest session so that before the end of the year we'll have a substantial amount of feedback to go through, filter, and introduce to the game. We'll have more on this in the next update. 

Right now, the tweaks, updates, and changes are touching up almost every single part of the game you can imagine. Here's a peek at one of the later levels visited by Palmer. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/56ca2cb2d2cf37841ce6f19ba6b81d761fead943.png[/img]
[i]Jump through those hoops[/i]

[h1]THE BADDIES[/h1]
David and Biro are reimagining monsters to more closely align them with the original vision of the game. This also means all of the baddies that you had fun shooting up are currently going through an in-universe version of the "Extreme Makeover". Based on your feedback we decided to take the designs closer to that of the original Warlock and better visual consistency. Chunky, lo-fi pixel consistency that is. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/27ab2bae9b46b81e90aee684b6e54ccd0ff058df.png[/img]
[i]The usual suspects - reimagined[/i]

Thicker outlines, blockier features, and additional color palettes bring the enemies closer to what you can expect from a Project Warlock game. We're very happy with the visuals you can already enjoy in the demo version of the game, yet we feel there is still some work to be done here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/3414b5c1b0f96a19d39596f8b69f98ca902282fa.gif[/img]
[i]Upgraded Shambler model  [/i]
 
[h1]THE LEVELS[/h1]
To follow through with the classic TV shows of the bygone era theme - what happened (and is still happening on daily basis) is the MTV Cribs-worthy amount of work that goes into reimagining levels in the game. Based on numerous messages we received from the backers, demo players, and friends David started reworking levels throughout the game. 

As he elegantly put it: "all levels have been adjusted in some way. Some of them have been reworked from the ground up with whole sections replaced or remade from scratch so they work better as a whole. All levels have improved lighting and refined textures. Level flow should be more natural and navigation more intuitive now."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/762f44b485fc0c39da5e9487f797fec835a09588.gif[/img]
[i]Castle Warlockstein[/i]

Another area undergoing the visual overhaul is the look of the watery surfaces. These now look like something that wouldn't feel out of place in Berserk's Eclipse setting, and one that should infuse the progression deeper into the Necromancer's domain with a sense of dread and unease.    

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/9efbd0b337023fc68821bd3f4123179f92f29b46.gif[/img]
[i]No shader liquids will flow[/i]

[h1]THE HUD[/h1]
To understand what happened to the HUD look no further than what was going on at Pimp my Car, only substitute spray paint with beautiful pixels. All the menus and in-game screens are still being conjured by the team just like in that show, just without all the fuss and Xzibit. Below you can find a tool-tip screen that - while still WIP - shows the direction that the game will take. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/3d240ccb673c0d81481d93f34d246faf3e0de544.png[/img] 
[i]New info screens[/i]

[h1]THE FACE[/h1]
Facial animation for Palmer? Also in the works. The team is nailing the finishing touches with the skill of our digital pixel surgeon Biro who undertook the procedure under the watchful eye of chief surgeon David. Take a peek under the bandages below. You know. Like Nip/Tuck.   

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/f3e2e85729484b3ec033ce3435317954d3f79e4f.png[/img]
[i]The looks that could (and will) kill[/i]

Now since Palmer is a character that displays a range of emotions - the image above is only a glimpse of what you will experience in-game. So please find below the Many Faces of Palmer as he's been subjected to the three key emotions defined by "The Definite Guide to the FPS Psychology" and known as: "default", "damage" and "smile", all across different ranges of bloodiness. 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/104b274189a5335f7f4c39f4bb3fb248eda2ab27.png[/img]
[i]Different states of Palmer[/i]

[h1]THE TOOLS[/h1]
The weapons also are getting a bit of polish and shine. Smoother animations, faster reload additional frames - all things that are noticeable but not necessarily at first glance. Just so you know - that these are getting retooled as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/e73df7f8024fef03302b02d32760c27b3699c376.png[/img]
[i]Some of the WIP arsenal laid bare[/i]

For more updates about the game, follow us on Steam and join our [url=https://discord.gg/ensxn8yTvd]Retrovibe Discord[/url]. Remember to wishlist the game, and tell your friends.

See you next time!

notes.title: Watch the dev play Project Warlock II demo!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

A couple of weeks ago we announced that [b]Project Warlock II[/b] will be featured on Steam Next Fest alongside hundreds of other exciting games…

And that day has come, and we have so much cool stuff in store for you! So get your weapons loaded and get ready so send some demons back to hell!

Last week we released an updated demo packed with new features! 

Have you ever wondered how awesome it would be to slay some demons with a Laser Rifle??? How about [b]TWO[/b] Laser Rifles???!!! 

We’ve added an [b]upgrade station[/b] to the demo level, which allows you to upgrade various weapons. For example, you can upgrade the Assault Rifle to a Laser Rifle, and combine it with Akimbo for ultimate carnage!

Apart from that, we have added [b]2 sliders[/b] to visual settings, so you can configure the graphics to your liking.

Another brand new feature is a combo counter that measures your demonslaying skills. Wanna get a bit competitive? Share your highest score on the [b][url=https://discord.gg/ensxn8yTvd]Discord[/url][/b]!

Apart from the updated demo we’ve prepared something else!

During Steam Next Fest you will be able to watch [b]Kuba [/b]from [b]Buckshot Software[/b] play the demo and share his stories about his work on [b]Project Warlock II[/b]. The show starts at 9:00 PM  CEST / 12:00 PM PT on October 1st!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/9e40549e5b3ea79f9afe93ddd885e1d2c738f417.jpg[/img]

We can’t wait to see you there and play our demo and also hear your feedback. Don’t hesitate to share your opinion on the [b]Community Hub[/b] forum or on our [b][url=https://discord.gg/ensxn8yTvd]Discord[/url][/b]!

That would be it for now. Stay on the lookout for more news about Project Warlock II. In the meantime enjoy the Steam Next Fest and squeeze as much as you can from the demo!

Remember to follow [b]Project Warlock II[/b] here on Steam, wishlist the game and tell your friends!

Until next time,
Retrovibe Games

notes.title: Project Warlock II Kickstarter update
notes.notes:
With just 5 days left, the [b]Project Warlock II[/b] Kickstarter campaign is entering its final phase. We thought it would be a perfect moment to update you on the progress the backers have made so far. And maybe you'll find something to your liking as well. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/2f4329cb9b27a3f01fc7bc46a5e9c6bae5ee67f1.png[/img]

In the last 3 weeks, more than 830 backers pledged over €26.000. We would like to thank all the backers for their immense support and love for our game.

This is the last week of the campaign, so if you would like to join us on this wonderful journey head to: 

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/project-warlock-2/project-warlock-2

Backers who support the game can get the "Backer" role on the Retrovibe Discord channel, Digital Early Access key for Steam, and - depending on the pledge level - can also receive additional items, such as: a boxed version of Project Warlock II. 

Right now 175 copies of the physical Project Warlock II found their owners, which means that the €50 Flap Box will contain additional items such as:
- a thicker manual,
- a sticker,
- a 32 page colour artbook,
- a collector’s pin,
- an 8GB Laser Rifle Pendrive

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/9f75247172546a3702ccfe1f30b2f3263bdb0493.png[/img]

Now the item that's still waiting to be unlocked is the Steel Book that needs 20 extra copies of the Boxed Edition sold. And this is what it looks like from up close. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/5e0df8460e7d33dfba56c5eddbccb2e88ca17743.png[/img]

On top of the unlocked contents of the Box Edition of [b]Project Warlock II[/b] there's also a couple of items you can order separately. 

The three available are:

- A [b]Project Warlock II[/b] themed mousepad 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/3366b151ed4905487cd76883e635d70d214d89d6.jpg[/img]

- A [b]Project Warlock II[/b] Hardcover Artbook

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/5c294b3977000f59d8b0723b4db30a196e3322ee.jpg[/img]

- A terrifying Shambler 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/ba16a429baeb28e468f89b2fd03033c76acb4e6b.jpg[/img]

Apart from physical rewards, we invite the most generous backers to help us design various elements of the game, such as spells, guns, monsters, and even a Warlock and a level in the PWII. Those rewards are limited, and some of them are no longer available (shoutout to those who decided to show such an immense amount of support!).

So what can you design in [b]Project Warlock II[/b]?

How about one of the spells in the game?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/29462b6a20a66ba5f9919f3dab8906a8f29920ff.jpg[/img]

Not really in the mood? Prefer to have a hand in creating something more substantial? How about...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/0832ea43dce4a5fd97b3283393680c999a5e19b5.jpg[/img]

Now let’s talk about stretch goals we’ve set to show our appreciation to all of you, and we decided to add new features to [b]Project Warlock II[/b] with each goal.

At €10.000 the Extra Narrative Illustrations reward was unlocked, meaning that you will see additional inter-mission artwork during your playthroughs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/b1fb08fac350da37d2ffbe201477ded85e2e3fa7.jpg[/img]

At €20.000 Alternate Weapon Skins for the Warlocks’ arsenal were unlocked. This will give you a chance to swap around weapon skins and make every playthrough feel a little bit different.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/f08e0ca26c30d8b6502d0f9777e25ff13928bb15.jpg[/img]

At €25.000 you unlocked Enemy Boss Voice Overs, which will add an extra depth of immersion to our game. We already have amazing ideas, and we can’t wait to get to work on the voicelines!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/cd74dfc677aeb743fb61fb545d2c3fe4e14ad716.jpg[/img]

As for further goals we have Photo Mode, Extra Enemy Variants and Arena Mode as well. 

We would, once again, like to thank all of the backers for the support, and the trust placed in us. The work on the game is well underway and we hope that you will love the game once it launches. The Kickstarter campaign might be coming to an end, but it’s only the beginning for [b]Project Warlock II[/b].

notes.title: Updated demo ver 0.1.5.15 out now
notes.notes:
Thanks a lot for the detailed feedback on the demo! You spoke, we frowned, we wanted to say "why don't you make your own game then", we recovered, gave it some extra thought and conceded you were right. So: here's what's going to change as of this update. Some nicely illustrated highlights first, and the full changelog right after that. 

We decided to open the curtains up a bit, as it's really dark in here, boy 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/4da82d6b078540d790f92cdf531c6a1fb1e923ab.png[/img]

And let's set you up with some nice, atmospheric fog for good measure 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/fd837d15fedd2eae796e6a3a1f4cf8bcd44cdef8.png[/img]

Problems with directions? Let's drop some more hints right there on the map then

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/d9c7f27af298393290da286e89dd7c3820fa45e2.png[/img]

There's now these little terminals that provide hints when you approach them

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/374442f48322ba89f57d1e58a5565b813379b319.png[/img]

The hints in all their raw glory 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/95609656170df5800285f3bfe10b17abd3a3213c.png[/img]

Full Demo 0.1.5.15 changelog below:

- [b]Added safety feature[/b] - the game will no longer freeze if the game does not have access to save/load folder. Instead, an error dialog will show up. The issue still might occur if the access to complete "Project Warlock 2" folder is read-only - we are still working on the issue
- [b]Increased Rifle Ammo Pack[/b] ammo from 20 to 25
- [b]Added additional Ammo Packs[/b] to early part of the level
- [b]Added sword pickup[/b] to the secret passage at start of the level
- [b]Moved the switch[/b] to the secret passage to a new place
- [b]Added Legend[/b] to Automap
- [b]Added Door[/b] and Interactable Elements icons to the Automap and Minimap
- [b]Adjusted player height[/b]. It was a bit too low compared to monsters
- [b]Akimbo pickup[/b] now replenishes ammo completely on pickup
- [b]Removed Physics from keys[/b]. They should not disappear anymore
- [b]Improved Lighting[/b] in the level
- [b]Added Tutorials[/b] to E1M1
- [b]Changed default key bindings[/b]. Interact is now E, quick save is F5 and quick load is F9
- [b]Increased monster aggressiveness[/b]
- [b]Added a slight delay[/b] when taking out a weapon which was not reloaded to encourage usage of other weapons

notes.title: Project Warlock II demo available now
notes.notes:
Two years of development. Total revamp of physics, visuals, level architecture, sound, music, enemy design, enemy fear, arsenal, spells systems, types of secret… 

Yeah, [b]Project Warlock II[/b] has gone a long way.

We are committed to bringing you the best game we can and the most open way about this is to simply have a demo available for you. Today.  

We can elaborate on each and every aspect, but there's probably only one question you really want answered: how does it play? 

Well - you better see for yourself. 

And please tell us what you think in the comments. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1640300/Project_Warlock_II/

notes.title: Weekend at Warlock's
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

This was a busy week for [b]Project Warlock II[/b], as we're nearing the moment where you will be able to play the game. Between working on the current build of the game and fixing bugs that tend to appear in soon to be released games, rethinking certain design choices thanks to supportive friends (hey, Dave!), working on the demo (what DEMO?), and finishing marketing activities we also took part in certain initiatives that you guys might find interesting  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/eba761182463e4b1a4bf373519b12bf7205e8693.jpg[/img]

1.	[b]Realms Deep 2021 event [/b]

[b]Project Warlock II[/b] was featured as a part of the #RD2021 event, where we debuted a gameplay video alongside 160 other excellent retro-themed games. This was also the first time ever we showcased a longer section of gameplay with no image and sound manipulation. So - the gameplay you see is taken from the actual build of the game dating around three weeks' ago (submission date). In the gameplay below you can see footage from Episode 3, halfway into Palmer’s adventure. You will be able to see spells in action, a lot of shooting and enemies that get bisected, blown to bits, shotgun-beheaded and filled with lead in their full pixelated glory. We aimed to show the game in it’s full on balls to the top action mode. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/dfdc7662420141cc0236bf1b2ae5e4f47c1ac9b3.png[/img]

2.	[b]Collector's Edition[/b]

That was the moment where we announced - amongst other things - [b]Project Warlock II[/b]'s Collector’s edition that's available right now. This is something you can get your hands on provided you like kicking things that are starting. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723470/9f75247172546a3702ccfe1f30b2f3263bdb0493.png[/img]

3.	[b]First ten minutes @IGN[/b]

On Sunday an exclusive preview of the first level in action (first ten minutes) aired on IGN showing the slightly tweaked version of the first level. Tweaked as in – having a Hard level amount of enemies with Standard difficulty level behaviour and health levels. The game is still in testing phases, but you can see the way [b]Project Warlock II[/b] currently plays. You can check out environments, gunplay, an upgrade and different effects showing the game in action. Played by no-one other than Kuba - @PWarlock_dev himself. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KI9tciXbcTY

4.	[b]Realm Deep 2021 The Vault video[/b]

Released after the actual Realms Deep event as a part of the in-depth videos filled section see below the video where Kuba takes you through the development of [b]Project Warlock II[/b]. This is a part of a larger collection of videos alongside other games in Realm Deep's website section of The Vault.  

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3lD2VmA5PsM

And that's... just the beginning. Watch this space for more!
